solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musicians in costume

definitions.meaning: a group of players performing together, as in a chamber group
a complete outfit of matching clothes worn together

explanation.surface: A band of players turning up in fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names both a performing group and a coordinated outfit, two senses of things that go together.

clue.text: Can he con criminal? Most unlikely!

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so the letters of these three words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a con man could ever be a crook: not a hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' reads as a description of the con man, but it signals the rearrangement of CANHECON.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of flat refusal or impossibility, just like saying something is extremely improbable.

clue.text: Outbreak of illness starting with revolting contaminated housing?

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold a single letter inside them, as a house holds its occupant
revolting is taken as turning over, so the phrase for contaminated is read backwards

parts.note: something contaminated is not pure

indicators.note: the starting letter of illness is the one taken

explanation.surface: A disease outbreak traced to filthy, disgusting accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns NOTPURE round to ERUPTON, and 'housing' puts I, from 'illness starting', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash or volcanic outburst is a sudden breaking out, so an eruption is a synonym of an outbreak.

clue.text: Drop ancient historian from audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken as it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an eighth-century English monk and historian

explanation.surface: An old chronicler is cut after trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb (dropping the historian), but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round globule of liquid, as of sweat, is a bead, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Log falling on leg in our canal

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second, as if it had fallen onto it

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A tree trunk drops onto someone's leg beside a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal of a human body is called by this anatomical term, so it is literally our internal canal.

clue.text: Buffoon Mark rejected old woman — that hurt!

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: to reject is to send back, so the two letters for the old woman are written backwards

parts.note: ma is a colloquial term for one's mother, an old woman
ouch is the exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A clown spurns a scarred old lady, who cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns MA into AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaramouche is the boastful, cowardly clown of the commedia dell'arte, hence any foolish jester figure.

clue.text: Secret society controlling racket from South island

indicators.note: the society takes control by holding the noise within its letters

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal secret society

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the south means read upwards, so the word is backwards

parts.note: a din is a racket or loud noise

explanation.surface: A gang running a southern scam on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'from South' means read upwards, giving NID; 'controlling' is the containment signal, the society holding the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger of the two Caribbean islands forming the republic with Tobago, so a specific example of an island.

clue.text: Reprimand right for academic

parts.note: to lecture someone is to scold them at length

explanation.surface: A telling-off that is deserved, delivered to a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A university teacher who gives talks is an academic, so the noun is a type of academic.

clue.text: Dark scene as small number go inside church

parts.note: No is the short form of number

indicators.note: the word for a go is placed within the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turn is a go, as in a game

explanation.surface: A gloomy tableau as a few people file into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small number' means the short written form of number, not a few people.
explanation.definitionFit: In painting the term names a night scene, as in Whistler's pictures, so a dark view.

clue.text: Insider from Acton wrestling to claim prize

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take hold of the prize, enclosing it
wrestling twists and contorts, so the letters of the place name are twisted around

parts.note: a cup is a prize, as in a trophy

explanation.surface: A wrestler from Acton, a London district, wins a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling' looks like the surface sport but scrambles the place name to OCANT; 'to claim' means hold, so the prize sits within.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in or sits inside a place is its resident, an insider in the literal sense.

clue.text: Soil fan finds truffle?

parts.note: earth is soil
a nut is an enthusiast or fan

explanation.surface: A gardening enthusiast digs up a prized fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the truffle is one thing called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to various underground tubers and also to the truffle fungus, which grows beneath the soil.

clue.text: Source of naval power in Rome gone after collapse

indicators.note: once something collapses it lies in a jumble, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Imperial Roman sea strength ended after the empire fell.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment holding a ship's motors is where its propulsive power comes from.

clue.text: Everyone choosing Princess to accept love note

indicators.note: the princess's name takes in the letter for love, holding it within

parts.note: Electra was a princess in Greek myth, daughter of Agamemnon
love is zero in tennis, written O
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A princess agrees to take a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' is the containment signal, making ELECTORA; 'love note' looks like a billet-doux but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of voters, all those choosing in an election, is collectively a nation's voting public.

clue.text: River current taking out both banks?

indicators.note: a river's banks are its edges, so the word's two outer letters are removed

parts.note: modern means current or up to date

explanation.surface: A river's flow cutting away at its banks on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a river's flow, but it means up to date, MODERN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Wind, destructive at the outset, coming in closer

indicators.note: the opening letter comes into the comparative word, sitting within it

parts.note: closer as in tight-fisted means stingier, meaner

indicators.note: only the outset, the first letter, of destructive is used

explanation.surface: A gale, ruinous at first, drawing nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as nearer, but it is tighter with money, MEANER; 'Wind' is the verb, rhyming with 'find'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander along a twisting course, like a river, is to wind, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Think to behave diplomatically? About time!

indicators.note: about here means around, so the verb wraps round the letter for time

parts.note: to mediate is to act as a go-between, behaving diplomatically

explanation.surface: Ponder whether to be tactful; and it's about time too!
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation of impatience, but 'About' puts T inside MEDIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect deeply or ponder, a synonym for think.

clue.text: At a country home being entertained

definitions.note: At is the chemical symbol of the element, so it stands for the element's name

indicators.note: the word for home is a guest inside the word for country

parts.note: a state is a country
in means at home

explanation.surface: A guest being hosted at a house in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a link word but it is the definition: the chemical symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: The radioactive halogen with atomic number 85 has the periodic-table symbol At.

clue.text: Bob, eg British coin: not good

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for good is left out of the coin

parts.note: the guilder was the Dutch currency coin before the euro

explanation.surface: A bob, an old British shilling, is a poor coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bob' was British slang for a shilling, the coin the surface suggests, but here it is Bob the Builder of children's television.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob the Builder is the children's cartoon character who constructs things, so he is an example of a tradesman.

clue.text: Refuse to provide exits

definitions.meaning: the noun, meaning leftovers or rubbish
departures, the acts of going away

explanation.surface: Declining to supply the ways out.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means scraps left behind, and also, read literally, the acts of departing from somewhere.

clue.text: Face headless man, drinking port

indicators.note: the shortened name drinks in the port, taking it inside
the man's name loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: Dexter is a man's name
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, often shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: Confronting a decapitated man who is downing fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink, but it is the Brazilian harbour city RIO; 'headless' trims DEXTER to EXTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer surface or front of something is its outside, so a face is its exterior.

clue.text: Sweet and flowing in poetic source

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed in the poetic word for a spring

parts.note: font is a poetic word for a spring or fountain, a source of water

indicators.note: flowing means moving freely, so the three letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Something lovely pouring from a spring in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' seems to describe the spring but scrambles the little word to NDA; 'in' places that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft creamy sugar paste used in confectionery and icing, so a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Information at short notice sent back

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: Details were returned at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short notice' looks like an idiom for little warning, but it is AD, a shortened advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for analysis are information, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Appliance, left out in the old days for bathroom cleaner?

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left comes out of the tool

parts.note: a tool is an appliance or implement

indicators.note: the word for the old days goes in the middle of the word the

parts.note: the past is the old days

explanation.surface: A device was left out of bathrooms in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L, leaving TOO; 'in' gives THPASTE. The question mark flags that this cleaner is for teeth, not tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the paste used to clean teeth, normally kept in the bathroom, so a playful description.

clue.text: Artist ultimately carried weight, though not initially in poor condition

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of the word artist is used
the phrase for carried weight loses its first letter

parts.note: if something carried weight it mattered

explanation.surface: An artist who once mattered, now down on his luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged and torn clothes or books are in bad shape, so the adjective means badly worn.

clue.text: Mistake to ignore leader in church area

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is dropped from the word for a mistake

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: It is wrong to overlook the head of a congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, so a particular part of a church.

clue.text: A two-page conclusion with one Times supplement?

parts.note: pp is the abbreviation for pages
the end is the conclusion
I is the Roman numeral one
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A short ending added to the newspaper's supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times supplement' suggests a section of this newspaper, but X is the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional matter attached at the back of a book is a supplementary section.

clue.text: Element in languages voiced by cardinal

indicators.note: voiced means spoken, so the word is taken as it is pronounced

parts.note: tongues are languages
ten is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: A churchman speaks in many languages about a basic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal with atomic number 74, also called wolfram, is a chemical element.

clue.text: Regularly target a certain masterpiece?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of target is taken

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Aim consistently at a great work of art, if you're sure.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a masterpiece is one kind of thing prized as this.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly valued object, such as a great work, is called a national gem or prized possession.
